$comment: How the host's autodeploy paces itself (root ADR-0159, ADR-0187). scripts/deploy/foundation-autodeploy.sh reads it from the control checkout the host trusts. quiet_minutes_after_a_deploy: after a deploy succeeds, the next one waits this long, then ships main's head with every commit merged meanwhile; operators and scheduled jobs get the host between deploys. A failed deploy leaves the running release as it was, so the commit that fixes it does not wait. deploy_attempts_per_commit and retry_after_minutes: how often, and how far apart, a failed deploy of one commit is tried again from the step that failed (root ADR-0597). A missing file means no quiet window.
quiet_reason: Measured 2026-10-17 18:30 to 10-19 03:36 UTC from the autodeploy journal: 45 deploys, the host inside a deploy 72% of the time, the median gap between deploys 2.1 minutes (24 of 44 under 5), one chain of 5 deploys over 136 minutes with no 5-minute gap, and half the deploys (22 of 45) shipping one commit. 15 minutes is the coordinator's choice of 2026-10-19; measure the same numbers again after it runs.
retry_reason: Root ADR-0597. Measured 2026-11-19..20 from the staging smoke's journal on ai-server: its database step (the same work every run, foundation_staging from empty through the schema chain) took 17 s to over 300 s, and 3 of 27 runs went over its 300 s limit (11-19 21:27Z, 11-20 04:44Z, 09:52Z); the next run of each passed (21:58Z, 06:03Z, 10:17Z). That is a failure rate of about 0.11 a run from the host's shared disk, not from the commit, so 3 attempts leave about 0.0014 for a passing commit, if the attempts are independent. 10 minutes apart is a decision, not a measurement: it lets the I/O burst behind one failure pass, and it keeps three attempts within about 30 minutes plus their own time. A commit that fails 3 times waits for a newer one, as every failed commit did before.
